| [TERM-106](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-106.md) v4 | reconfiguration slack: the temporary resources a system needs to move between two configurations it can each hold, beyond what holding either one requires, while keeping specified commitments | A's proposal, from the pasted synthesis on constraint architectures (pasted by the owner on 2026-11-04, continuing the exchange on emergency readiness whose share link could not be fetched), Part 4. A's definition: "temporary resources required to move between otherwise feasible organizational regimes while preserving specified commitments". Made exact here as the gap between the bottleneck budget of a transition and the larger of its endpoints' holding requirements, infinite when no admissible path joins them. It folds in A's "resource-constrained reconfiguration", the name of the inquiry rather than a concept, and A's three reserves (operational, reconfiguration, competency), of which the second is what is held to meet this slack. What is held to meet it, the reconfiguration reserve, is a special case of organizational slack: measured against current output it is slack, and its use is the transition, which the output does not show. The wording is A's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Active |
